reference.title: Cable Seated Crunch
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching; drawn facing the high pulley with the rope at the head)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl down, breathe in as you come back up.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s down, short squeeze, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can curl down with the hips still for every rep.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower return

cues.text: Sit tall on the end of a flat bench facing the high pulley, feet flat a little wider than the hips. Hold the rope ends beside your head at the temples, elbows in front.
Breathe out and curl the ribs toward the pelvis, bringing the elbows down toward the knees. The hips stay on the bench.
Squeeze the abdominals at the bottom; the hands stay at the head and do not pull.
Breathe in and uncurl slowly back to sitting tall, keeping tension on the cable.

mistakes.mistake: Rocking the whole trunk forward from the hips
mistakes.fix: Keep the pelvis still on the bench; curl the spine one section at a time.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the rope down with the arms
mistakes.fix: Lock the hands at the head; let the trunk move them.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the stack pull you upright fast
mistakes.fix: Return over about 2 s and stop before the weight touches down.

mistakes.mistake: Tucking the chin hard to the chest
mistakes.fix: Keep a fist-width gap between the chin and chest; the neck follows the trunk.

kinematics.norm: From sitting tall to the ribs curled toward the pelvis, elbows coming down onto the front of the thighs; no study fixes the angle (clinical opinion)
Lumbar and thoracic flexion with the pelvis still (clinical opinion); about 3 degrees of lumbar flexion in a floor crunch, cited by Escamilla 2016 from earlier work, so this curl is larger
Pelvis and legs still on the bench; the seat removes the hip hinge (clinical opinion)
Rope held at the head, arms passive (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Seated Crunch, video (movement reference)
Escamilla, Lewis, Pecson, Imamura and Andrews 2016, muscle activation among supine, prone and side position exercises with and without a Swiss ball (Sports Health 8(4):372-379; PMC4922527)
Axler and McGill 1997, low-back loads over a variety of abdominal exercises: searching for the safest abdominal challenge (Med Sci Sports Exerc 29(6):804-811)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain in the back or neck.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep.
Loaded spine flexion raises low-back compression; people with disc problems may prefer non-flexion core work (McGill 1998, clinical opinion).
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Neck strain: keep the chin a fist width from the chest and the hands still at the head.
Low-back discomfort: smaller range, lighter load.

muscleNotes.core: Prime mover: rectus abdominis curls the ribs toward the pelvis against the cable and controls the return.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help flex the trunk and keep it from twisting.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help flex the trunk and keep it from twisting.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Hold the upper arms still so the hands stay at the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Hold the upper arms still so the hands stay at the head (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Sit tall, rope at the head

guides.label: Head and hands curl down together
